summary: PATH hijack of `node` via bin name collision triggers shim execution during dependency postinstall
details: Package declares `bin.node` pointing at `shim.js`. On `npm install`, npm symlinks this entry as `node` into `node_modules/.bin` and prepends that directory to PATH while running lifecycle scripts of sibling dependencies. The package depends on `esbuild`, which has a postinstall script; when that postinstall invokes `node`, the symlinked shim runs in place of the real Node interpreter, achieving arbitrary code execution against the installer at install time. The shipped shim demonstrates the primitive by writing a marker file to `/tmp/.bunnyhijack-test`, but the mechanism would execute any code the shim contains. The package's own description self-identifies as a proof-of-concept of this technique.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
